headline: Water department shares Kīhei desalination study, hears resident concerns

meeting.summary: The water department shared desalination study options costing $119 million to $328 million, with construction 10 years or more away.
meeting.recap: The water department presented findings of a study on desalination, which means removing salt from water.[[0:00:05]] Staff said the central and south Maui water system has been short on water sources for many years.[[0:06:30]] The study recommended reverse osmosis, a proven filter technology.[[0:21:42]] It recommended injecting the leftover salty brine into deep wells.[[0:23:33]] One option is a brackish water plant starting at half a million gallons a day, expandable to two million.[[0:24:53]] Its estimated building cost is $119 million at half a million gallons a day, or $261 million at two million.[[0:25:44]] A four million gallon a day seawater plant would cost an estimated $328 million to build.[[0:26:17]] Staff said construction would be 10 years or more away.[[0:28:31]] A resident urged focusing on efficiency and infrastructure instead of desalination.[[0:44:32]] Another resident said they should seek any federal funding available for this.[[1:02:46]]
meeting.next: If the community gives support, the department could select a site and apply for federal funding. The department will post the presentation on its website. People can send questions or comments to an email address shown at the meeting. A consultant said a deeper study of the underground rock and water would be done for injection sites. Staff said they are wrapping up this year's water availability analysis for the central system.
